# Sandscale

> Isolated Firecracker microVMs for AI agents, with Vault, DLP, approvals and a tamper-evident audit log built in. Memory included.

Sandscale runs the code AI agents write in sandboxes, workspaces, build hosts and lab hosts, each its own Firecracker microVM. Use it from the TypeScript SDK (Python coming soon), the `sandscale` CLI (macOS and Linux), the REST API or the remote MCP server at mcp.sandscale.dev. Hosted in the US; Europe is coming soon. Sign up free at https://cloud.sandscale.dev/auth/signup. Every page below is also available as Markdown at the linked .md address, and pages are served as Markdown to requests with `Accept: text/markdown`. All docs in one file: https://sandscale.dev/llms-full.txt

## Docs

- [Docs](https://sandscale.dev/docs.md): Sandscale developer docs. Start a sandbox for the code your agents write, give coding agents a persistent cloud computer, and keep every run governed and audited.
- [Using the API](https://sandscale.dev/docs/api.md): How to call the Sandscale API, the hosts, request and response format, identifiers and where to find each endpoint.
- [Authentication](https://sandscale.dev/docs/api/authentication.md): Authenticate to the Sandscale API with a personal API key or your own sign-in. Key scopes, expiry, rotation and revocation.
- [Errors](https://sandscale.dev/docs/api/errors.md): How the Sandscale API reports a refused request, the error body, the status codes and the error codes you meet on many endpoints.
- [Limits and retries](https://sandscale.dev/docs/api/limits.md): Rate limits, plan quotas and how to retry Sandscale API requests safely.
- [Agent Cloud](https://sandscale.dev/docs/concepts/agent-cloud.md): Sandscale Agent Cloud gives coding tasks to agents running in your workspaces, lets you watch them live, and returns a branch and pull request.
- [Approvals and policies](https://sandscale.dev/docs/concepts/approvals.md): Sandscale approval gates and policies on templates, sizes, run times and which agents may run. Approvals on every plan.
- [Audit log](https://sandscale.dev/docs/concepts/audit.md): Sandscale keeps a hash-chained audit log of every action. Every plan can read it; Team and Enterprise can export it as evidence.
- [Build hosts](https://sandscale.dev/docs/concepts/build-hosts.md): Sandscale build hosts are clean, leased build machines for agent tasks, released when the task ends.
- [Lab hosts](https://sandscale.dev/docs/concepts/lab-hosts.md): Sandscale lab hosts connect your own Linux or macOS machines, with their hardware, so a run can claim them. Team and Enterprise.
- [Object storage](https://sandscale.dev/docs/concepts/object-storage.md): Sandscale object storage is S3-compatible storage for files, datasets and build artifacts that outlive a run. United States now; Europe coming soon.
- [Regions](https://sandscale.dev/docs/concepts/regions.md): Sandscale runs in the United States now; Europe is coming soon. One account, with your workloads and their data kept in the region they run in. API hosts api.sandscale.dev and api.us.sandscale.dev.
- [Sandboxes](https://sandscale.dev/docs/concepts/sandboxes.md): A Sandscale sandbox is a Firecracker microVM for the code your agents write, with its own kernel and the network access your plan allows.
- [Teams and SSO](https://sandscale.dev/docs/concepts/teams-and-sso.md): Sandscale organizations, invitations, roles, groups and SSO on Team; SCIM, verified domains and custom roles on Enterprise; passkeys and multi-factor sign-in on every plan.
- [Vault](https://sandscale.dev/docs/concepts/vault.md): Sandscale Vault keeps secrets out of prompts and logs. Secrets are referenced, injected at run time and never placed in prompts or logs.
- [Workspaces](https://sandscale.dev/docs/concepts/workspaces.md): A Sandscale workspace is a persistent cloud computer for coding agents and people. Files survive, you open it in the browser or over SSH, and it stops when idle.
- [Lease a build host with the API](https://sandscale.dev/docs/guides/build-hosts-api.md): Lease a build host from a pool, connect over SSH with a short-lived certificate, run and record commands, renew and release the lease.
- [Connect Claude or ChatGPT](https://sandscale.dev/docs/guides/connect-claude-chatgpt.md): Add mcp.sandscale.dev as a remote MCP connector in Claude, ChatGPT or any remote MCP client and run sandboxes from chat, with your own sign-in.
- [Store files in object storage](https://sandscale.dev/docs/guides/object-storage.md): Create a Sandscale object storage bucket and an S3 access key, find your region's S3 endpoint, and use standard S3 tools and SDKs.
- [Run code in a sandbox with the API](https://sandscale.dev/docs/guides/sandboxes-api.md): Start a sandbox, run commands, move files in and out and stop it, with the Sandscale HTTP API.
- [Pause, resume and snapshot a sandbox](https://sandscale.dev/docs/guides/snapshots.md): Pause a Sandscale sandbox and resume it later, save its /workspace as a snapshot, and start new sandboxes from it.
- [Give a run a secret](https://sandscale.dev/docs/guides/vault-secrets.md): Store a secret in Sandscale Vault once and give it to a sandbox as an environment variable, without the value passing through your code, the API answer or a log.
- [Work in a cloud workspace](https://sandscale.dev/docs/guides/workspaces.md): Create a Sandscale workspace from a template, open it over SSH or in the browser, forward ports, set a schedule and stop it, with the CLI or the SDKs.
- [Quickstart](https://sandscale.dev/docs/quickstart.md): Sign up for Sandscale, create an API key, run a command in a sandbox with the TypeScript SDK, connect Claude Code, Codex or Cursor over MCP, and pick a region.
- [SDKs](https://sandscale.dev/docs/sdks.md): The Sandscale SDKs for TypeScript and Python: install, authenticate, pick a region, start a sandbox and run a command, handle errors and retries.
- [Python SDK](https://sandscale.dev/docs/sdks/python.md): Every method and option of the Sandscale Python SDK (sandscale 0.2.0), generated from its source.
- [TypeScript SDK](https://sandscale.dev/docs/sdks/typescript.md): Every method and option of the Sandscale TypeScript SDK (@sandscale/sdk 0.2.0), generated from its source.

## Product

- [Agent Cloud](https://sandscale.dev/agent-cloud.md): Give coding tasks to agents running in your workspaces, watch them live, and get a branch and pull request back. A lead agent can run the team through one MCP address.
- [Build hosts](https://sandscale.dev/build-hosts.md): Lease a large, clean Linux machine for the heavy part of an agent’s work. Access and secrets end with the lease and the host is wiped.
- [Leases](https://sandscale.dev/build-hosts/leases.md): Your agent leases a large, clean host from a pool for the heavy part of its work. Access and secrets end with the lease, and the host is wiped.
- [CLI](https://sandscale.dev/cli.md): The sandscale command line for macOS and Linux: sandboxes, workspaces, snapshots, SSH, terminals and MCP.
- [Integrations](https://sandscale.dev/integrations.md): Connect coding agents to Sandscale over MCP, script it with the CLI, or call the API. SSO with SAML or OpenID Connect, SCIM on Enterprise, and workers in your own AWS account on Enterprise.
- [Lab hosts](https://sandscale.dev/lab-hosts.md): Connect your own Linux and macOS machines with security keys, TPMs, debug probes and boards. Runs claim a device, a person approves when policy says so, and it is released when the run ends.
- [Device policy](https://sandscale.dev/lab-hosts/device-policy.md): Write down which devices each project may claim, which claims need a person to sign off, and who that person is. Anything you didn’t allow is refused.
- [Object storage](https://sandscale.dev/object-storage.md): S3-compatible object storage for files, datasets and build artifacts that outlive a run. Works with standard S3 tools and SDKs. US now, Europe coming soon.
- [Regions](https://sandscale.dev/regions.md): Where Sandscale runs: US East (N. Virginia) on AWS now, Europe (Frankfurt) coming soon, or your own AWS account on Enterprise. What stays in your region and what is held in the US.
- [Europe region](https://sandscale.dev/regions/eu.md): Sandscale in Europe (Frankfurt, Germany) on AWS eu-central-1: what runs there, what stays there, and the rules organisations there work under.
- [United States region](https://sandscale.dev/regions/us-east.md): Sandscale in the United States (N. Virginia, United States) on AWS us-east-1: what runs there, what stays there, and the rules organisations there work under.
- [Sandboxes](https://sandscale.dev/sandboxes.md): A Firecracker microVM for every agent run, with network access you control. Every prompt and tool call recorded and checked against your policy.
- [Files in and out](https://sandscale.dev/sandboxes/files.md): Move a source tree into a sandbox and pull reports, builds and logs back out, up to 1 GiB per file.
- [Live output](https://sandscale.dev/sandboxes/live-output.md): Run a command in a sandbox and read stdout and stderr as they happen, then the exit code, from the CLI, the API or your agent.
- [MCP server](https://sandscale.dev/sandboxes/mcp.md): Connect Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any MCP tool to the Sandscale MCP server and it can create a sandbox, run commands in it, move files and throw it away, every call on the record.
- [Pause and resume](https://sandscale.dev/sandboxes/pause-and-resume.md): Pausing keeps a sandbox’s memory and files. Resuming brings it back as it was, so an agent can stop for the night and carry on in the morning.
- [Snapshots](https://sandscale.dev/sandboxes/snapshots.md): Save a sandbox after the slow part, like installing dependencies, and start new sandboxes from that point instead of from scratch.
- [SSH certificates](https://sandscale.dev/sandboxes/ssh.md): Open a shell in a sandbox or workspace with a certificate that expires in minutes, issued to you and recorded in the audit log.
- [Authenticated tunnels](https://sandscale.dev/sandboxes/tunnels.md): See the app or API your agent started inside a sandbox, from your own machine, through a tunnel that only you can open.
- [Warm pools](https://sandscale.dev/sandboxes/warm-pools.md): A warm pool keeps sandboxes from a template already booted, so when your agent asks for one it gets a running microVM straight away.
- [Templates](https://sandscale.dev/templates.md): Sandbox templates pinned by image digest: every sandbox started from a template gets exactly the same bytes. Start from Python, Node.js, Go or Rust, or your own image.
- [Workspaces](https://sandscale.dev/workspaces.md): A persistent cloud machine for Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI. Close your laptop and the agent keeps working; open the same session from any device.
- [Editors and devices](https://sandscale.dev/workspaces/editors.md): Open your workspace in the browser, or point VS Code, Cursor or a terminal at it. The agent’s session lives there, so you can close the laptop and pick it up anywhere.
- [Schedules and idle sleep](https://sandscale.dev/workspaces/schedules.md): Start and stop workspaces on a schedule, and let them sleep when nobody uses them. The disk stays; hours count only while they run.

## Pricing and programs

- [Open source](https://sandscale.dev/open-source.md): Sandscale Pro free for 6 months for maintainers of active open-source projects: sandboxes, workspaces and build hosts for your CI and agents.
- [Pricing](https://sandscale.dev/pricing.md): Sandscale plans: Free, Pro $20 a month, Team $40 per member a month, and Enterprise. Included awake vCPU-hours every month; paused and idle time is free.
- [Startups](https://sandscale.dev/startups.md): Sandscale Team free for 6 months for startups: monthly credits cover your Team subscription.

## Security

- [Security](https://sandscale.dev/security.md): How Sandscale contains agent code and proves it: a Firecracker microVM per run, network controls, Vault, DLP on prompts and tool calls, human approvals, SSO and SCIM, a hash-chained audit log and compliance evidence.
- [Agent policy](https://sandscale.dev/security/agent-policy.md): Claude Code runs under your policy through its hooks: each prompt is checked, and each tool call is allowed, blocked or sent to a person. Codex and Gemini CLI report every step.
- [Approvals](https://sandscale.dev/security/approvals.md): When policy says a call needs sign-off, the agent waits while a person approves or denies it. An approved call runs once.
- [Audit log](https://sandscale.dev/security/audit-log.md): Every sandbox, command, approval, secret and change is written to an audit log where each entry is chained to the one before it, so an edit shows.
- [Vulnerability disclosure](https://sandscale.dev/security/disclosure.md): How to report a security vulnerability in Sandscale, what to include, and what happens after you report it.
- [DLP on prompts and tool calls](https://sandscale.dev/security/dlp.md): On every plan, prompts and MCP tool calls are scanned before they go anywhere, so a credential pasted into a prompt never reaches the model.
- [Evidence export](https://sandscale.dev/security/evidence-export.md): Every audit entry for a period, its hash chain checked, packed into one file you hand to your assessor.
- [Roles](https://sandscale.dev/security/roles.md): Give people Viewer, User, Editor or Manager on each sandbox, template and project. Whoever starts a sandbox owns it.
- [SSO and SCIM](https://sandscale.dev/security/sso-and-scim.md): Sign in with SAML or OpenID Connect through Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace or any standard identity provider, and keep members in step with your directory over SCIM.
- [Vault](https://sandscale.dev/security/vault.md): Keys and tokens live in Vault and reach a sandbox, workspace or build host in memory, for as long as the run lasts.
- [Signed webhooks](https://sandscale.dev/security/webhooks.md): Send sandbox events to your own endpoints, signed so you can check they came from Sandscale, and retried if your endpoint is down.
- [Your own cloud](https://sandscale.dev/security/your-own-cloud.md): Sandscale workers can run in your own AWS account, through a role you create with an external ID. No long-lived keys, and your data stays in your account.

## Blog

- [Blog](https://sandscale.dev/blog.md): Sandscale news, releases and how-tos, written plainly.
- [An incident runbook for AI agents: stop, scope, rotate, review, resume](https://sandscale.dev/blog/agent-incident-response-runbook.md): A copy-and-adapt runbook for when an AI agent does something it should not: who does what in the first minutes, how to find out what it touched, which credentials to rotate, and how to bring agents back safely.
- [Five ways agent sandboxes are billed, and what each one charges while your agent waits](https://sandscale.dev/blog/agent-sandbox-billing-models-compared.md): Per-second provisioned resources, active CPU plus provisioned memory, active-only CPU with provisioned memory and disk, per-second VMs, and awake vCPU-hours. How each published meter treats the minutes an agent spends waiting on a model, with sources.
- [Agent sandbox glossary: 41 terms in plain English](https://sandscale.dev/blog/agent-sandbox-glossary.md): Plain definitions for the words that come up when you run AI agent code in isolation: microVM, VMM, KVM, jailer, gVisor, seccomp, namespaces, egress allowlist, lease, snapshot, warm pool, awake vCPU-hour and more.
- [Turning an exported, verifiable log into evidence for your own assessment (no certification claimed)](https://sandscale.dev/blog/audit-evidence-for-soc2-from-agent-logs.md): Your auditor will ask how you control AI agents. How to turn an agent platform's audit log into evidence an assessor can test: map entries to the Trust Services Criteria, prove the population is complete, pick periods, and keep the chain of custody.
- [What an audit log for AI coding agents should record](https://sandscale.dev/blog/audit-log-for-ai-coding-agents.md): What to log for every coding agent run, from who started it to secret use and DLP hits, why each field matters in an incident review, and where Sandscale's audit log covers it and where it does not.
- [Awake-time billing for agent sandboxes: what you pay for and what you don't](https://sandscale.dev/blog/awake-time-billing-agent-sandboxes.md): How Sandscale bills agent sandboxes by awake vCPU-hours: paused and idle time don't burn vCPU-hours, storage still bills. Includes a worked example with the arithmetic shown.
- [The best AI agent sandboxes in 2026: 14 options and how to choose](https://sandscale.dev/blog/best-ai-agent-sandboxes-2026.md): A sourced field guide to AI agent sandboxes as of November 2026: E2B, Modal, Daytona, Vercel, Cloudflare, Fly.io Sprites, Freestyle, Morph Cloud, Northflank, Sandbox0, Beam, PandaStack, Temps and Sandscale. Five questions, best-for lines, one table, FAQ.
- [When a job needs a leased machine instead of a sandbox, from the live docs](https://sandscale.dev/blog/build-hosts-vs-sandboxes.md): Sandboxes and build hosts solve different problems. How to tell which one a step of an agent's work needs, what a lease adds (pools, approvals, SSH certificates, a hard expiry), and how to move only the heavy step without moving the agent.
- [A sandbox API client in Go with net/http and context deadlines](https://sandscale.dev/blog/calling-the-sandbox-rest-api-from-go.md): Run code in a Sandscale sandbox from Go using only the standard library: typed requests and results, errors with codes and request IDs, and context deadlines that respect a command's own timeout.
- [Calling the Sandscale sandbox API from Python with requests, no SDK](https://sandscale.dev/blog/calling-the-sandbox-rest-api-from-python.md): A small Python client for the sandbox REST API: start a sandbox, write files, run a command, read results, stop it, and turn error responses into exceptions you can act on.
- [Canary tokens in agent sandboxes: tripwires that tell you when a run goes rogue](https://sandscale.dev/blog/canary-tokens-for-agent-sandboxes.md): Plant fake credentials and hostnames where a misbehaving agent would look, and get an alert when they are used. How to place canaries in agent runs, what each kind detects, and how to avoid false alarms.
- [Taking an agent's changes out of the sandbox as a patch, and checking it before it touches your repo](https://sandscale.dev/blog/checking-an-agent-patch-before-applying.md): A coding agent that works in a sandbox should hand back a patch, not push a branch. How to produce a binary-safe patch inside the sandbox, and a TypeScript check on your side that refuses symlinks, renames and oversized diffs and flags CI, hooks, dependencies and agent instruction files for a person.
- [Claude tool use with a Sandscale sandbox: the whole loop in one file](https://sandscale.dev/blog/claude-api-tool-use-with-sandscale.md): A complete tool-use loop with the Anthropic TypeScript SDK where Claude's run_command and write_file calls execute in a Firecracker sandbox. Tool schemas, tool_result blocks with is_error, a turn limit and cleanup. Type-checked.
- [A sandbox for Claude Code: running it headless in a cloud workspace](https://sandscale.dev/blog/claude-code-headless-in-a-cloud-workspace.md): Run Claude Code with claude -p inside a Sandscale workspace, a persistent Firecracker microVM, so its Bash tool works on a cloud disk instead of your laptop. Setup, permission flags and what stays where.
- [Cloudflare Sandbox alternatives: options when your agent does not live in a Worker](https://sandscale.dev/blog/cloudflare-sandbox-alternatives.md): Cloudflare Sandboxes run container instances behind a Worker, with lifetime tied to Durable Object activity. Alternatives for standalone APIs, long waits, bigger boxes, built-in governance and persistence, with a sourced table and FAQ.
- [A sandbox for Codex: running codex exec in a cloud workspace](https://sandscale.dev/blog/codex-exec-in-a-cloud-workspace.md): Run OpenAI Codex non-interactively with codex exec inside a Sandscale workspace, a persistent Firecracker microVM, and drive it from your laptop over SSH. Sandbox modes, JSON output and schedules.
- [Running Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI under policy on Sandscale](https://sandscale.dev/blog/coding-agents-under-policy-sandscale.md): Two ways to run coding agents on Sandscale, what policy enforces for Claude Code versus what it only records for Codex and Gemini CLI, and the gaps.
- [Queueing agent runs against a concurrency cap: backpressure, fairness and limit errors](https://sandscale.dev/blog/concurrency-limits-and-queueing-agent-runs.md): Every sandbox platform caps how many boxes run at once. A TypeScript queue that respects the cap, shares it fairly between users, tells a full queue from a refused start, and stops when waiting will not help.
- [Four container escapes and what they teach about running agent code](https://sandscale.dev/blog/container-escape-cves-lessons-for-agent-sandboxes.md): runc CVE-2019-5736, Leaky Vessels, Dirty Pipe and CVE-2022-0185: how each one worked, why it mattered for shared-kernel isolation, and what to take from them when your AI agent runs code.
- [CrewAI agents that run code in a Sandscale sandbox, over the REST API](https://sandscale.dev/blog/crewai-tools-on-sandscale-rest-api.md): Give a CrewAI crew BaseTool subclasses that run commands and write files in a Firecracker sandbox through Sandscale's REST API with requests. A developer and a reviewer share one box per crew run, cleaned up in finally. Checked against crewai 1.15.
- [Custom sandbox templates: give your agent's sandboxes your toolchain, pinned by digest](https://sandscale.dev/blog/custom-sandbox-templates-pinned-by-digest.md): Build your own image, pin it by digest and register it as a Sandscale sandbox template with sandscale sandbox template init and build, then start sandboxes from it. When a template beats a snapshot or a setup script.
- [Data residency for agent sandboxes: what stays in a region, what is global, and what to ask](https://sandscale.dev/blog/data-residency-for-agent-sandboxes.md): When an agent runs code on customer data, 'where is it processed?' has several answers: the sandbox, its files and output, the model call, logs, the audit trail and the account. A map of each, and the questions to put to any vendor.
- [Daytona alternatives in 2026: picks for microVM isolation, open source, persistence and GPUs](https://sandscale.dev/blog/daytona-alternatives.md): Daytona defaults to containers, moved core development private in 2026 and sets limits by tier. When each of those matters, here are the alternatives, with best-for lines, a sourced table and an FAQ.
- [Designing a run_code tool for an LLM: schema, limits and results a model can act on](https://sandscale.dev/blog/designing-a-run-code-tool-schema.md): The JSON Schema, description and result shape for a code-execution tool, field by field: what to expose, what to cap, how to report timeouts and refusals so the model does the right thing next, and a TypeScript handler.
- [DNS exfiltration explained: how data leaves a network that blocks outbound traffic](https://sandscale.dev/blog/dns-exfiltration-explained.md): An egress allowlist that blocks HTTP but lets the sandbox resolve any name still leaks. How DNS exfiltration works, why recursive resolvers carry it, the controls that stop it, and how to test your own setup.
- [E2B alternatives in 2026: where to go and why, by workload](https://sandscale.dev/blog/e2b-alternatives.md): E2B is a solid Firecracker sandbox. Here is when something else fits better: governed coding agents, stateful workspaces, snapshot and branch, GPU work, your own hosts. Sourced table, best-for picks and FAQ.
- [Designing an egress allowlist for agent sandboxes](https://sandscale.dev/blog/egress-allowlist-design-for-agent-sandboxes.md): How to decide what code your AI agent runs is allowed to reach: start from nothing, find the hosts a task really needs, and avoid the DNS, CDN and wildcard traps.
- [The Firecracker balloon device: reclaiming guest memory, and why it is not a limit](https://sandscale.dev/blog/firecracker-balloon-device-explained.md): How Firecracker's virtio balloon works: target size, deflate_on_oom, statistics, free page reporting and hinting, and the security caveat that a compromised guest driver can ignore it.
- [What a Firecracker guest needs: kernel image, root filesystem, boot arguments and devices](https://sandscale.dev/blog/firecracker-guest-kernel-and-rootfs.md): A walkthrough of the pieces a Firecracker microVM boots from: vmlinux or bzImage, guest kernel configs and the support policy, an ext4 rootfs with an init, boot arguments, drives, and the optional vsock, entropy and balloon devices.

- [Integration tests for agent tools that run code: fixtures, cleanup, labels and budgets](https://sandscale.dev/blog/testing-agent-tools-against-real-sandboxes.md): Unit tests with a mocked sandbox miss the bugs that matter: timeouts, output limits, missing tools in the image, network refusals. How to write a small integration suite against real sandboxes that is fast enough to run in CI and never leaves boxes behind.
- [A threat model for AI coding agents: what can go wrong, and where to put the controls](https://sandscale.dev/blog/threat-model-for-ai-coding-agents.md): A practical threat model for coding agents: the assets at risk, the ways untrusted text gets in, the attacker goals, and which control belongs at which layer.
- [Three clocks: setting sandbox, command and request timeouts for AI agents](https://sandscale.dev/blog/timeouts-for-agent-sandboxes.md): An agent sandbox has three separate time limits: how long the sandbox lives, how long one command may run, and how long your client waits for an answer. How they interact, and how to set each one.
- [Feeding command output back to an LLM: truncation, cleanup and secret masking](https://sandscale.dev/blog/truncating-tool-output-for-llms.md): Raw tool output is the wrong shape for a model's context: too long, full of terminal noise, and sometimes full of secrets. A TypeScript helper that normalizes, masks, collapses and truncates output before the model sees it.
- [Getting code into a sandbox and results out: files, folders and change lists](https://sandscale.dev/blog/uploading-a-project-into-a-sandbox.md): Three ways to move code into a Sandscale sandbox, single files, whole folders as a tar archive, and reading files back, plus how to ask which files the agent changed.
- [Use case: an agent that turns a bug report into a failing test](https://sandscale.dev/blog/use-case-bug-reproduction-agent.md): Designing an agent that reads an issue, reproduces it in an isolated sandbox started from a snapshot of your repo, and hands back a failing test and a patch for a person to review, with the controls that keep it safe on public issues.
- [Use case: a code interpreter for a chat product, one sandbox per conversation](https://sandscale.dev/blog/use-case-chat-code-interpreter.md): How to back a chat assistant's code interpreter with one Firecracker sandbox per conversation: lifecycle across turns with pause and resume, files in and out, per-user labels, limits, and what to tell the model.
- [Use case: evaluating a coding agent across many tasks, one sandbox per attempt](https://sandscale.dev/blog/use-case-coding-agent-evals.md): Running agent evals in isolated sandboxes: a shared starting snapshot, one box per task attempt, hidden tests copied in after the agent finishes, concurrency within plan limits, retries, labels and cost accounting.
- [Use case: an agent that upgrades dependencies and proves the tests still pass](https://sandscale.dev/blog/use-case-dependency-upgrade-agent.md): A design for a dependency-upgrade agent that runs each upgrade in its own sandbox with registry-only network access, fixes breaking changes, runs the tests and hands back a reviewed patch, plus the supply-chain controls it needs.
- [Use case: telling flaky tests from broken ones with parallel sandboxes](https://sandscale.dev/blog/use-case-flaky-test-detection-in-parallel-sandboxes.md): Run a failing test many times across several fresh Firecracker sandboxes started from the same snapshot, and get a verdict: stable, broken or flaky, with timeouts and memory kills reported separately. Useful for CI and for coding agents. Type-checked TypeScript.
- [Use case: grading code submissions from strangers, one microVM per submission](https://sandscale.dev/blog/use-case-grading-untrusted-code-submissions.md): Designing an autograder or coding-exercise judge on sandboxes: per-submission isolation, no network, hidden tests copied in after the code, time and memory verdicts from the run result, output caps, and what to log.
- [Use case: a coding agent that keeps working after you close the laptop](https://sandscale.dev/blog/use-case-long-running-agent-in-a-workspace.md): Running Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI inside a Sandscale workspace instead of on your machine: setup with the CLI, attaching from any device, schedules and idle stop, what to give the agent, and when a sandbox or Agent Cloud fits better.
- [Use case: testing the code snippets in your docs, one sandbox per page](https://sandscale.dev/blog/use-case-testing-docs-code-snippets.md): Docs examples rot quietly. Extract the snippets you mark as testable, run each page's snippets in order in a fresh Firecracker sandbox, and fail CI when one breaks. A type-checked TypeScript runner with concurrency kept within your plan.
- [Use case: a text-to-SQL agent that queries a read-only copy in a sandbox](https://sandscale.dev/blog/use-case-text-to-sql-agent-on-a-sandboxed-copy.md): Let a model answer questions with SQL without giving it your database. Copy a SQLite extract into a Firecracker sandbox, open it read-only, cap rows, and return results as JSON to a Vercel AI SDK tool. Type-checked, with the runner tested.
- [Vercel AI SDK tools backed by a Sandscale sandbox](https://sandscale.dev/blog/vercel-ai-sdk-tools-on-sandscale.md): A TypeScript integration guide: three AI SDK tools (run_command, write_file, read_file) that act on one Firecracker sandbox per task, with output caps, path checks, a step limit and a guaranteed stop.
- [Vercel Sandbox alternatives: when to look past it and where to go](https://sandscale.dev/blog/vercel-sandbox-alternatives.md): Vercel Sandbox runs Firecracker microVMs metered on Active CPU. Alternatives for teams not on Vercel, needing bigger boxes, built-in agent governance, GPUs or self-hosting. Best-for picks, sourced table, FAQ.
- [WebAssembly or a microVM for agent-written code? A comparison from the projects' own docs](https://sandscale.dev/blog/wasm-vs-microvm-for-agent-code.md): WebAssembly runtimes and microVMs both promise to run untrusted code safely, in very different ways. What each boundary is, what code each can run, and which fits the code AI agents actually write.
- [What DLP on LLM prompts catches, what it misses, and what to layer around it](https://sandscale.dev/blog/what-prompt-dlp-catches-and-misses.md): Pattern-based scanning of prompts and tool calls stops pasted API keys and known token formats. It misses encoded, split and unformatted secrets, and everything inside the sandbox. A practical look at the strengths, the blind spots and the layers that cover them.
- [Writing a policy for coding agents: a plain-English template you can adapt](https://sandscale.dev/blog/writing-a-policy-for-coding-agents.md): An example policy for Claude Code, Codex and similar agents, in three lists: allowed on its own, needs a person, never. With the reasoning behind each line and how such a policy maps to hooks and approvals.
